title: Token Zen Map — compact, role-aware token cost explorer + export
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a compact, role-aware token-cost explorer called 'Token Zen Map' that surfaces per-route and per-session token breakdowns, attribution, and export flows in a small-panel, embeddable widget for the Redwood Console. Focus on: compact density for dashboards, role-specific presets (Dev/Finance/Support), and a frictionless CSV/Parquet export that preserves attribution lineage.
rationale: Customers ask for quick at-a-glance cost attribution inside dashboards and rollouts without a full drill-down. Existing token cost UIs are dense and require multiple clicks. Token Zen Map aims to be an inline, export-ready view for both engineers (latency/cost tradeoffs) and finance (chargeback-ready CSV), enabling faster incident triage and consumption-based billing conversations.
user_stories: As an engineer, I want to open a route dashboard and instantly see the per-invocation token composition and recent cost trend so I can evaluate optimization wins.
As a finance analyst, I want to export a compact, audit-friendly CSV that includes prompt IDs, model variant, quantization profile, and per-token cost attribution for chargeback.
As a support engineer, I want a role-presets toggle (Dev / Ops / Fin) so the panel highlights the metrics I care about without reconfiguring filters.
design_notes: Panel must render within dashboard compact column (min 300px width). Primary viz is a horizontal stacked-sparkline showing token categories (system, prompt, response, kv-cache hits) plus a micro-sankey on hover to show attribution to route/endpoint. Export should include: session_id, prompt_hash, tokens_by_category, model_variant, quant_profile, cost_usd, timestamp, and parent_request_id when available.
decisions: Use sampled recent 10k invocations for realtime rendering to keep query latency <500ms (decision: sampling).
Expose role-presets as shallow state tied to user role + per-dashboard overrides (decision: preserve per-dashboard overrides).
Export format: CSV primary, Parquet advanced option for enterprise (decision: dual-format export).
review_comments: PM (Lina Torres): Suggest adding a small RAG indicator (cost delta vs baseline) to make regressions visible at a glance.
Eng (Ben Choi): Backend needs a compact index for prompt_hash -> tokens_by_category to support export; flagged as dependency ENG-18455.
Security (Priya Rao): Exports must honor PII redaction policy; ensure prompt text is not exported unless explicitly allowed via export-scopes (commented).
tradeoffs: High-density compact view prioritizes synopsis over exhaustive telemetry. We will sacrifice per-token timing granularity in favor of rendering speed and export fidelity. Sampling reduces accuracy for long-tail invocations but keeps costs and latency predictable. Providing Parquet increases implementation complexity but necessary for enterprise chargeback workflows.
tasks: Finalize NPM components for stacked-sparkline and micro-sankey (Design -> Eng handoff).
Define export schema and map to billing ledger fields (Finance + Eng).
Implement backend sampled index endpoint and export job (ENG-18455 assigned).
Add RAG delta indicator and QA accessibility (contrast/compliance).
Create docs and console help text describing export lineage and privacy controls.
acceptance_criteria: Panel renders inside Route dashboard at 320px width with stacked-sparkline + category legend.
Hover micro-sankey shows attribution to route/version and samples up to 20 representative sessions.
CSV export contains required fields and matches billing ledger columns; Parquet export available behind enterprise flag.
Role-presets toggle applies immediately and persists per-user, with ability to override at dashboard level.
Export respects PII redaction and obeys export-scopes; audit event is written to console logs for each export.
